# Generated files carry no version

**The question.** Which version of the generator rendered this package? The
obvious place to answer is a line in every generated file's header.

**Decided.** The generated files name no version. Their header is
`// Code generated by nightseam. DO NOT EDIT.` and stays that way; the tool
reports its version, `nightseam version`, and its output does not carry it.
[The generator](../declaration/generator.md#which-version-rendered-this).

**Why.** A version in the header would rewrite every generated file of
every consumer on every release, which the golden discipline would feel
immediately, and it would fail a `check` over output that is otherwise
byte-identical — which is the failure the `version` command exists to
explain, not one to add. When a `check` disagrees across two machines,
`nightseam version` on each is what answers why; the output itself
answering would have made the disagreement.

**Serves.** Declarative — what is derived is derived from the declaration
alone, and a derivation is stale only when the declaration or the tool's
rendering changed, never when its number did.

**Since.** 0.3.0.
